hypothesis: Within the fixed Q7 quintet-scoring grammar, formula complexity (number of included feature families) is positively associated with the strict-prior ranking percentile of the realized quintet on the next target.
primary_estimand: Mean per-target Spearman correlation between formula feature_count (1..10) and normalized percentile score across all 1,023 formulas, over the Blind OOS targets.

target_protocol.eligible_target_indices: 101..3386 inclusive (100 scored-target burn-in retained for exact comparability with Q141-B6)
target_protocol.strict_prior: For target index t, formula scores/ranks must be computed from draws strictly before t; the target outcome is used only to evaluate the already frozen rank.
target_protocol.target_update_order: score target, write rank row, then add target draw to state

metric_definitions.spearman: Per-target Spearman correlation with average ranks for ties; average across targets within split.

registered_tests.endpoint: Blind OOS mean per-target Spearman rho
Blind OOS mean percentile across all formulas
Blind OOS high-complexity minus low-complexity mean percentile
Blind OOS high-complexity minus low-complexity Top-20 rate

inference.multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni across the four registered Blind OOS endpoints
inference.discovery_validation: descriptive split comparison; no winner selection or parameter tuning

interpretation: This is a fixed-grammar retrospective walk-forward test of a structural complexity association, not a deployable selector and not proof that the draw is predictable. Holm covers only these four registered endpoints, not the entire Q00-Q141 research family.
decision_rule: No claim of complexity usefulness unless the primary Blind OOS effect is at least 0.02, its Holm-adjusted one-sided p-value is below 0.05, and the result is not contradicted by the registered controls.
